Marcus / Team —

Quick take after modeling:
- 6mo exclusivity (NA HealthTech) is high precedent risk. It limits partner motion; recommend limiting to a 90-day exclusivity for pilot only, tied to a strictly defined list of partner accounts and maximum ARR cap ($250k).
- Benchmark clause as written (automatic 25% product discount if throughput >2.5x) creates open-ended margin loss. Recommend converting to a capped rebate: if benchmark met, Optima gets a one-time credit equal to 12% of booked pilot spend (not a recurring product discount) and a right to negotiate a pilot-to-enterprise commercial uplift with Deal Desk review.
- 18% committed discount: that's > our standard mid-market guaranteed. Recommend counter of 10% for a 12-month committed spend with a 1.2x minimum utilization clause and a non-cancellable minimum spend.

Legal redlines attached (redline_optima_sow_v2.docx) with suggested language for exclusivity carveouts (existing partners and marketplace listings), termination on material partner conflicts, and a clear metric spec for the benchmark (how latency/throughput are measured, sampling window, instrumentation).

If there is an executive exception request, outline below for signoff:
- Exception: Allow 90-day pilot exclusivity (NA, HealthTech) + capped benchmark credit (one-time 12% of pilot ARR) + 10% committed discount for 12 months with 1.2x utilization minimum.
- Business rationale: strategic reference customer in HealthTech; high technical validation; likely to expand into enterprise; faster time-to-revenue with exclusivity may accelerate adoption across other accounts.
- Risks: sets precedent for niche exclusivity asks; potential partner churn; discount dilutes unit margins.

Recommend Rishi signoff on exception (term + cap) if leadership accepts the capped credit approach.

-Ben
